info.title: aimem hub API
info.description: The complete HTTP surface of an aimem hub (and of the local service, which serves the same mux over a unix socket without auth). Every route except the three public pages (/, /v1/status, /admin) requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; routes marked x-role admin additionally need an admin token (the env token, or a tokens.json entry with role admin). This spec documents the surface and its auth contract; request/response bodies are intentionally loose (JSON objects) - the store types in internal/store are the authority on field shapes. A parity test (openapi_test.go) fails CI when this file and the real route table disagree. A request carrying X-Aimem-Team-Context is served only on the routes marked x-team-mode, after online verification; every other route refuses it with team_operation_unsupported (403) before aicrew is contacted, and it is never served as a personal request. A team-mode request that did not arrive over TLS terminated by the hub is refused first, with tls_required, whatever forwarded headers claim.

post.summary: Redeem an enrollment subcode for one user-scoped token, delivered encrypted
post.description: enrollment.v1 §3 (docs/DESIGN-AIFORGE-ENROLLMENT-WIRE.md). No bearer is evaluated: the subcode in the body is the authority. One transaction creates one user with no grant and one user-scoped token, sealed with HPKE (hpke-x25519-sha256-chacha20poly1305) to the client's public key; the bearer is never sent in clear. An identical retry (same subcode, Idempotency-Key and input) replays for 1 hour after the redemption, also past the subcode's expiry; another key or other input is enrollment_conflict (409). Unknown, expired, revoked, wrong-hub and no-longer-replayable subcodes are all enrollment_invalid (403). At most 10 requests per minute per client address and 20 per subcode (rate_limited, 429). Requires TLS terminated by this hub (tls_required) and X-Aimem-Enrollment-Version: 1. The answer is no-store. Not exposed as an MCP tool.

Refusals use the envelope with active_mode team: context_unavailable (503, retryable), context_stale, identity_mismatch, grant_denied, role_forbidden (403). In team mode this is the context report: mode, the verified team session (service, team, agent, role, session, generation, handle expiry), the projects the profile currently grants, task_write ("triage" for the coordinator role, false for every other role), knowledge read (the pilot's recall and shared-document reads on those projects) and doc_write "report-*" (the documents team mode writes); with ?project=<id> it adds project_read for that project.

get.summary: The project's repository (kind, clone URL, its host, access)
get.description: The one repository a project's work happens in, a hub property next to the process reference (docs/DESIGN-AIFORGE-PILOT-1.md §1). It holds no secret: the host of the clone URL, with its port when the URL names one (forge.example.org:3000), names the credential a member needs. An ordinary user token needs a live grant on the project (the knowledge-read rule); an unknown project answers as one without a grant. A team session reads it under its profile's live grant (grant_denied otherwise, ?history refused with invalid_request). `repository` is null when none is set. ?history=1 (admin only) adds the recorded changes, newest first, each with its action (project.repository.set or project.repository.clear), time, actor and the values before and after.

post.description: A partial update for triage (docs/DESIGN-AIFORGE-PILOT-1.md §4): only the named fields change, and every other field is kept. Body: expected_revision (the revision you read) and at least one of state (BACKLOG or READY; the task must itself be BACKLOG or READY) and next_action. Requires Idempotency-Key. A stale revision is 409 with the current task; a managed task or a task under an active reservation is 409. Ordinary user tokens may call this route under the ordinary task-write check. In team mode only a session whose verified role is coordinator may call it, on a project its profile is granted: another role is refused with role_forbidden, an ungranted project with grant_denied, and a task under a reservation with task_held (409, not retryable while the hold stands); the actor is the member's user. Tasks have no priority or size fields yet; triage gains them when they exist.

put.summary: identity.v1 team.register: aicrewd names its own team on the hub
put.description: identity.v1 team.register (docs/DESIGN-AIFORGE-PILOT-1.md §3): only an aimem_peer_ credential issued for team.register, for the path's service, may call this; every other credential is refused with peer_forbidden. Creates the peer's profile for an aicrew team UUID (lowercase canonical form), or renames it; renaming to the same name changes nothing. It never creates or touches a grant and never re-enables a disabled profile. Refusals: invalid_request (malformed UUID or name), peer_forbidden (another operation's credential, or a team UUID registered under another peer), team_name_taken (409: another team of this peer holds the name), profile_disabled (403: the operator disabled the profile; only the operator re-enables it). Every outcome, refusals included, is audited with the peer, the team, the old and new name and the outcome. Requires TLS terminated by this hub (plain HTTP, a TLS-terminating proxy and the unix socket are refused with tls_required) and X-Aimem-Identity-Version: 1. Bounded with the read scope at 60 calls per minute per credential (rate_limited). Not exposed as an MCP tool.

get.summary: identity.v1 board.read: the task state changes of the calling peer's teams' granted projects
get.description: identity.v1 board.read (aicrew's control-plane design, A0): only an aimem_peer_ credential issued for board.read, for the path's service, may call this; every other credential is refused with peer_forbidden. Returns {changes, cursor, more}: each change is {project, task_id, revision, from, to, at, required_capability}, the state a revision set and the state before it ("" for a creation) and the task's required capability at that revision ("" for the project's own), across every project granted to the calling peer's enabled team profiles. No task content. The cursor is opaque and bound to the peer; the same cursor reads the same page while nothing new is written, and reading on from the returned cursor never skips or repeats a change. A malformed or foreign cursor is invalid_cursor; a cursor past a project's last change is cursor_ahead. limit is 1 to 500 (default 100). Audited as board.read. post.description: Admin route: the bearer gate refuses ordinary tokens and storage refuses any non-admin actor. Enabled project required. Idempotency-Key required. One JSON body <=64 KiB; unknown fields and trailing values rejected; identical retries return the original receipt. Body: expected_generation as observed, token_id of the replacement token (issued to the session's user, live, with write scope for this project; verified against the access database) and reconciliation {old_credential_stopped:true, reason, runtime_check, evidence_refs}. Effect in one transaction: the session binds to the replacement token, its generation advances (and the coordinator generation for a coordinator), a reserved non-offer attempt follows the new generation as on resume with its lifecycle message, and an audit event records the transfer. The old credential can use no handle afterwards; receipts recorded under it never replay for the replacement, so an uncertain old command is re-read, not retried. A recorded operator assessment: nothing here stops a process. Responds with the session view like resume.
